FAQs page · Booking

How much does it cost?

Pricing is bespoke and quoted per event. It depends on which services you book, the size of the line-up, the running order and the travel involved, so there is no fixed price list. Send us your event details and we will quote against them.

FAQs page · Booking

Can we book more than one service?

Yes, and most events do. Booking singers, dhol and a DJ together means the handovers between them are planned in advance rather than improvised on the night, which is the most common failure point when performers come from separate suppliers.

FAQs page · Services + Ladies Sangeet

Are all your Ladies Sangeet performers female?

Asked on 2 pages. The answers are worded differently. Check both say the same thing, or tell us which page should keep it.

Answer on: FAQs page

The singers who lead a Ladies Sangeet are female. Accompanying musicians, including dholki players, are not always. If the evening needs to be women only throughout, tell us when you enquire and we will confirm what we can arrange for your date.

Answer on: Ladies Sangeet

The Sangeet singers who lead the evening are female. Accompanying musicians, including dholki players, are not always. If the evening needs to be women only throughout, tell us when you enquire and we will confirm what we can arrange for your date.

FAQs page · Services + Dhol Players

What is a dhol?

Asked on 2 pages. The answers are worded differently. Check both say the same thing, or tell us which page should keep it.

Answer on: FAQs page

The dhol is a double-headed drum from Punjab, played with two sticks and worn on a strap so the player can move with a procession. It produces the driving rhythm associated with bhangra and Punjabi celebration.

Answer on: Dhol Players

The dhol is a double-headed drum from Punjab, played with two sticks and worn on a strap so the player can move. It produces the loud, driving rhythm associated with bhangra and Punjabi celebration, and because it is portable it can lead a procession.

Ladies Sangeet

Can we choose our own songs?

Yes, and we would encourage it. The set list is built with you in advance from traditional Punjabi folk, boliyan, Pakistani classics, Bollywood and modern fusion. Specific family songs can be written into the running order, and songs you would rather avoid can be left out. Custom song selections are standard rather than an upgrade.

12

Ladies Sangeet

Do you provide dholki players?

Yes. Live dholki accompaniment is part of a Ladies Sangeet booking, and it is the thing that separates a Sangeet from a playlist. The dholki is the small two-headed hand drum the singing is built on, and the player works with the singers rather than simply keeping time.

13

Ladies Sangeet

Can you perform at a Mehndi or dholki night?

Yes. In most families the dholki night and the Sangeet are the same evening under two names, so if you are booking a dholki night, this is exactly the service that covers it. We also perform at Mehndi nights, where the format works well because guests are seated for long stretches while henna is applied, and at Jago celebrations, engagement parties and women’s community events.

Punjabi DJ

What music does a Punjabi DJ play?

A mix of Punjabi, Bollywood and international tracks. In practice the set is sequenced to move between traditional folk classics, Bollywood and current chart and Punjabi releases, so each part of the room gets its moment.
